title: JD Vance Weighs Skipping 2028 Presidential Race After Republican Midterm Losses, CNN Reports
excerpt: CNN, citing roughly a dozen allies and advisers, reported that Vance has seriously considered not running in 2028 after the November 3 midterm losses, but has made no decision and set no timeline.
body:
• Vice President JD Vance has given serious consideration to not running for president in 2028, people close to him told CNN, after Republicans' sweeping losses in the November 3 midterm elections.
  • CNN, citing interviews with roughly a dozen allies and advisers, reported that Vance has not made up his mind, has set no timeline, and that a White House bid remains firmly on the table.
  • Allies told CNN the war with Iran is the largest obstacle: if it is still happening, they question whether any Republican can win in 2028.
  • For voters, nothing has been decided: some allies are adamant it is more likely than not that Vance runs, and other Republicans, including Ron DeSantis, Ted Cruz and Brian Kemp, are already moving toward the race.

Vice President JD Vance has given serious consideration to not running for president in 2028 after last week's midterm elections, people close to him told CNN. The report, published on Friday, November 13, is based on interviews with roughly a dozen allies and advisers. It describes a vice president wrestling with his political ambitions, the fracturing of the MAGA coalition and the demands of fatherhood, and it stresses that no decision has been made.

What the report says — and what it does not

CNN reported that Vance, once considered the clear 2028 frontrunner, has not set a timeline for a decision and that a White House bid remains firmly on the table. Some allies told CNN it is more likely than not that he runs. Others were less certain. One person close to Vance said: "I wouldn't be surprised by any decision he makes. He's only 42. He's young enough that he can have a comeback should this environment make success impossible. It just may not be his time."

People close to Vance told CNN he entered the year uncommitted, and the arrival of his fourth child this summer had already fuelled speculation inside the White House that he might put his presidential ambitions on hold. More recently, CNN reported, his deliberations have centred on whether he — or any Republican — can win in the political climate President Donald Trump has created.

The Iran war at the centre of the calculation

Allies told CNN that the war with Iran may be the greatest obstacle to Vance's ambitions, and that much may depend on whether Trump can bring the conflict to a swift conclusion.

"The question isn't if JD can do it. It's: If the Iran war is still happening, can any Republican do it? If they don't end the war in Iran, no Republican has a shot at 2028."

— A Vance ally, speaking to CNN

The clearest public sign of Vance's thinking came the morning after the midterms, when he posted a lengthy message on X blaming the Republican losses on the war. "The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," Vance wrote, according to CNN. Sources told CNN the post irritated Trump, who, according to two people familiar with the discussions, was privately critical that Vance did not publicly stand by the decision to enter the war. A White House official told CNN the White House was aware of the post before it went out and that Trump had been briefed beforehand. On Thursday, according to CNN, Trump told Vance to stand down from leading Iran negotiations and instead focus his attention on corruption.

Counter-currents: allies urging him to run

The reporting is not one-directional. Terry Schilling, president of the American Principles Project, told CNN it would be a mistake for Vance to forgo a run out of political expediency. "He's basically teed up to be the general and we're going into one of the biggest battles," Schilling said. "I would be surprised if he doesn't run." Pollster Rich Baris told CNN the Republican brand has lost credibility with many Trump supporters — "MAGA is dead," he said — but argued Vance remains the Republican best positioned to pick up the pieces.

CNN also reported that polls showed essentially every faction that helped elect Trump in 2024 pivoted away this year, including men, young people, Latinos and white non-college educated voters.

What happens next

Other Republicans have already made moves toward 2028, including Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, Texas Senator Ted Cruz and Georgia Governor Brian Kemp, according to CNN. CNN reported that a donor network aligned with Vance, the Rockbridge Network, met in Houston this week to begin regrouping while awaiting his decision. Trump, for his part, has not said he will endorse his vice president. Asked by "60 Minutes" whether he would eventually make an endorsement, Trump replied, according to CNN: "Probably — not necessarily." For now, the only confirmed position is Vance's indecision itself.
